verdict.rationale: Mastra documents persisting execution state to storage: snapshots capture what is needed to resume a workflow exactly where it left off, and agents or workflows can be suspended and later resumed. Time travel can also re-execute from any step using stored snapshot data. However, the evidence frames resume around deliberate suspend/resume rather than automatic recovery after a crash or process restart, and snapshots are described mainly for workflows rather than general agent runs. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of crash/restart recovery of in-flight runs, agent-level (non-workflow) checkpointing, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can checkpoint agent state so a run can resume exactly where it left off after a crash or restart

citations.quote: Mastra uses storage to remember execution state, so you can pause indefinitely and resume where you left off.
Snapshots capture all the information needed to resume a workflow from exactly where it left off
Use resume() to restart a suspended workflow from the step where it paused.
Time travel allows you to re-execute a workflow starting from any specific step, using either stored snapshot data or custom context you provide.
